# Stream-page date distribution — 16 September 2026

**Research note.** The text-only stream pages generated by `edition_pages.py preview`
(`256t/editions/incident-preview/{huggingface,gemstuffer,wiki}.html`) show sharply clustered
date distributions. This note records the distributions and proposed explanations, for the
clusters and for the absences. Measured against `editions/three-stream/incident/windows.json`
and the manuscript on this date: 297 pages, 590 panels.

**Method caveat.** Each panel is counted at its clock **start**. Interval beats — panels dated
only to a span — land in their start day's bucket. Spikes are therefore overstated and gaps
understated: the 9 July HuggingFace spike includes panels spanning 9–13 July
(`hf-impact-boundaries-*`, `hf-search-noise-*`), and the 13 May cluster is six `may-replies-*`
beats spanning 13–26 May — the span covers part of what looks like an empty stretch.

## Distributions

### HuggingFace — 414 panels, 26 distinct dates, 20 Apr → 27 Jul

| Phase | Dates | Panels |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Prehistory | 20 Apr; 7–13 May; 26 May | 36 |
| June buildup | 4, 11–12, 17, 26–27, 29 Jun | 39 |
| Incident response | 4–7 Jul | 30 |
| Core cluster | 8–13 Jul | 243 (59%) |
| Second wave + coda | 16, 19, 27 Jul | 52 |

Peak day 9 Jul (94 panels; 74 of them interval beats). Longest true gaps: 20 Apr→7 May (16
days), 13→26 May (12 days, partially spanned by `may-replies-*`), 17→26 Jun (8 days),
19→27 Jul (7 days).

### GemStuffer — 58 panels, 10 dates, 5 May → 9 Jul

42 of 58 panels fall on 11–13 May. Then near-silence: 26 May→18 Jun (22 empty days) and
18 Jun→6 Jul (17 days). The July pair is `gs-cache-report` / `gs-cache-fix` — advisory and
deployment dates, not campaign activity.

### Collusion Wiki — 118 panels, 6 dates, 17 May → 22 Jun

110 panels on 19–22 Jun; 85 on 19 Jun alone. All second-precision. The 19 Jun cluster is a
roughly two-hour mass-deletion burst (`cw-wage-main-01..30`, `cw-wage-backup-01..10`,
12:40–14:44 UTC export preferred times) plus enrollment delete/return cycling; 20–22 Jun is
heartbeat and Dorfwiki-link aftermath. Twenty-five empty days precede the burst
(24 May→19 Jun).

## Proposed explanations for clusters

1. **Real event bursts.** The 19 June wiki deletion ran about two hours; 8–13 July is the
   intrusion's active phase plus the response it triggered; 11–13 May is the actual
   GemStuffer campaign window. Dense days partly reflect genuinely dense events.
2. **Log-structured sources produce event-shaped clusters.** `CW-EXPORT` is a
   reqlog/rclog/write_date export — every recorded request becomes a second-precision panel.
   The wiki stream's density is the log's density; it can only show days the export recorded
   relevant events.
3. **Retrospective reports cluster at reported granularity.** `METR` beats are mostly
   day/range precision — they land where the investigation stated a date. `GS-REPORT`
   (September attribution) can only assert days or ranges, so its beats bunch into the
   11–13 May interval it established.
4. **Contemporaneous timestamps create precision spikes.** `GS-STATUS` updates, the `OAI-TR`
   event table and `CW-EXPORT` logs produce minute/second clusters exactly where a live
   record existed (12–13 May status incident; 11 and 19 July event-table entries).
5. **Publication dates masquerade as event dates.** `gs-socket-analysis` panels are dated
   13 May — the day Socket published, not when specimens executed. `gs-cache-*` and
   `hf-hardening-account` (27 Jul, `HF-TL`'s own publication day) mark when things were
   written down or deployed.
6. **Interval-span inflation.** Beats known only to a span count at span start (see method
   caveat); single-day spikes partly aggregate multi-day spans.

## Proposed explanations for absences

7. **Forensic recovery, not surveillance.** `HF-TL` is a *recovered* chronology — its
   admission notes the recovered earliest event need not be the first event. The sparse
   April–May prehistory is what recovery retained; gaps are unrecovered time, not
   demonstrated quiet.
8. **Source scope limits.** `CW-EXPORT`'s grades cover requests and logged changes; idle
   wiki state leaves no record. The 25-day gap means no logged in-scope events — the edition's
   own reading rule applies: an empty frame means nothing is depicted, not that nothing
   happened.
9. **Attribution ceilings.** `GS-REPORT` frames 5 May as "earliest in the researchers'
   attribution" and discloses unknown theft success. The stream's late-May onward thinness
   tracks what investigators could attribute, possibly including genuinely dormant periods.
10. **Narrative handoff between streams.** Wiki activity ends 22 Jun; GemStuffer's last
    panels are 6–9 Jul; `hf-rubygems-staging` lands 13 Jul. Some absences are where the
    record's focus — and its sources — moved to a different row.
11. **Editorial selection.** Only source-registered beats enter the manuscript; gaps also
    reflect what has not been researched or cannot be shown.
12. **Institutional disclosure lag.** Every major source was published after the events
    (`HF-TL` 27 Jul is earliest; `METR`, `OAI-TR`, `OAI-OV` late Aug; `GS-REPORT` 11 Sep).
    The whole distribution maps evidence density — where institutions later chose or managed
    to document — more than raw event density.

## Summary

Clusters are mostly real bursts amplified by log-granularity sources; absences are mostly
evidence absence amplified by retrospective, span-granular sourcing. The two are hard to
separate, and the interval-page mechanism is the edition's way of keeping them honest.
